headline: A quiet beginning
development: The embryo is settling into the lining of the uterus and the neural tube — the future brain and spine — is starting to form. Two tiny layers of cells are already organizing into everything your baby will become.
momTip: If you haven't started a prenatal vitamin with folate yet, now is the moment — it matters most in these early weeks.
partnerTip: Celebrate the news together in a small, private way — this is your shared secret for now.

headline: First flickers
development: The heart is beginning to take shape and may pulse for the first time this week. The brain and spinal cord are forming from the neural tube.
momTip: Nausea can start now — keep plain crackers by the bed and eat something small before you get up.
partnerTip: Take over the cooking if smells start bothering her; an unscented kitchen is a real gift right now.

headline: A heartbeat, almost
development: Little buds that will become arms and legs are appearing, and the heart is beating in a steady rhythm. Facial features — eyes and a tiny nose — are starting to form.
momTip: Fatigue is your body doing serious construction work; nap without guilt.
partnerTip: Handle the grocery run and stock up on whatever plain foods she's actually willing to eat.

headline: Doubling by the day
development: Your baby has doubled in size since last week. Tiny hands and feet are emerging from paddle-shaped limbs, and the brain is growing by roughly a hundred cells a minute.
momTip: Sip water steadily through the day — dehydration makes nausea and headaches worse.
partnerTip: Learn one new thing about this week of pregnancy and share it with her — it shows you're in it together.

headline: Fingers and toes begin
development: Fingers and toes are forming, and the eyelids are starting to cover the eyes. Your baby is making small, spontaneous movements you can't feel yet.
momTip: If your first ultrasound is around now, bring tissues — seeing that flicker is surprisingly emotional.
partnerTip: Go with her to the first ultrasound if you possibly can; ask the questions she's too overwhelmed to ask.

headline: All essential parts
development: All the essential organs have begun to form, and the tail at the base of the spine is disappearing. Tiny earlobes and the tip of a nose are taking shape.
momTip: Your clothes may start feeling snug at the waist — a hair tie through the button loop is the classic trick.
partnerTip: Offer a back rub before bed; her body is working around the clock even while she sleeps.

headline: Officially a fetus
development: This week the embryo graduates to fetus. Vital organs are formed and starting to function, and tiny nails are beginning to grow on fingers and toes.
momTip: If morning sickness is peaking, cold foods often smell less — try chilled fruit or yogurt.
partnerTip: Keep a running note on your phone of snacks she can tolerate, and keep them stocked.

headline: Hiccups and stretches
development: Your baby is stretching, somersaulting, and even hiccupping — all in secret. Tooth buds are forming beneath the gums, and the diaphragm is developing.
momTip: Consider scheduling any first-trimester screening tests your provider recommends this week.
partnerTip: Start reading up on the screening options so the two of you can decide together, calmly.

headline: Reflexes in rehearsal
development: Reflexes are kicking in — your baby's fingers can open and close, and the mouth makes sucking motions. The intestines are moving into place inside the abdomen.
momTip: Many parents share their news around now; there's no wrong time, only your time.
partnerTip: If you're announcing soon, plan a reveal that feels like the two of you — not like anyone else's.

headline: Vocal cords, quietly
development: Vocal cords are forming, and your baby has tiny fingerprints on fingers the size of grains of rice. The placenta is fully up and running.
momTip: The second trimester is near — many people feel their energy return in the next few weeks.
partnerTip: Notice and name the small wins: the first day without nausea is worth a toast (sparkling water counts).

headline: The golden trimester
development: Welcome to the second trimester. Your baby can squint, frown, and may have started sucking a thumb. The kidneys are producing urine and the liver starts making bile.
momTip: With energy returning, gentle movement like walking or prenatal yoga can feel wonderful.
partnerTip: Plan a low-key date while energy is good — a walk, a breakfast out, an afternoon movie.

headline: Sensing the light
development: Though the eyes are still fused shut, your baby can sense light. The ears are nearly in their final position, and the skeleton is hardening from cartilage into bone.
momTip: Round ligament pain — a quick sharp tug on one side — is common now; move slowly when changing positions.
partnerTip: Remind her that new aches are usually just stretching; a heating pad on low and your hand on her back help.

headline: Listening in
development: The ears are developed enough that your baby may begin to hear muted sounds — your heartbeat, your voice. The circulatory system is fully operational.
momTip: Talk or hum to your belly when it feels natural; your voice will be the most familiar sound in your baby's world.
partnerTip: Start talking to the bump now — your voice is lower and carries well through the womb, and babies recognize it after birth.

headline: Growing a layer of cozy
development: Your baby is starting to build a layer of fat beneath the skin, and the umbilical cord is getting thicker and stronger. Sweat glands are beginning to develop.
momTip: Sleep on your side with a pillow between your knees — it's kinder to your back and circulation.
partnerTip: If she's started shopping for a pregnancy pillow, surprise her by researching the good ones.

headline: Yawns in the dark
development: Your baby is yawning, stretching, and flexing those brand-new muscles. The nervous system is wiring up at astonishing speed, and myelin — the insulation around nerves — is starting to form.
momTip: The mid-pregnancy anatomy scan usually happens around now — it's the longest, most detailed look you'll get.
partnerTip: Be at the anatomy scan. Seeing the spine, the heart chambers, the tiny profile together is unforgettable.

headline: A waxy little coat
development: A protective, cheese-like coating called vernix is covering your baby's skin. The senses — taste, smell, hearing, sight, touch — are all developing in their own dedicated brain regions.
momTip: If you haven't felt movement yet, it often starts soon — like bubbles, or a fish turning over.
partnerTip: Keep your hand on the bump in the evenings; in a few weeks you'll feel what she feels.

headline: Halfway home
development: You're at the halfway mark. Your baby is swallowing regularly and producing meconium, the first bowel movement. Those first flutters may now feel like unmistakable kicks.
momTip: Your appetite may surge — keep protein-rich snacks handy so the hunger works for you.
partnerTip: Mark the halfway point: a photo, a letter to the baby, or simply a long dinner talking about names.

headline: Tasting dinner
development: Your baby swallows amniotic fluid flavored by what you eat — an early education in the family menu. The bone marrow has taken over blood cell production from the liver and spleen.
momTip: Heartburn often shows up now; eat smaller meals and stay upright for a while after eating.
partnerTip: Take over dish duty after dinner so she can put her feet up immediately — heartburn hates that.

headline: Lips and eyebrows
development: Your baby's lips and eyebrows are distinct now, and the eyes are fully formed though the irises still lack color. Tiny tooth buds for adult teeth are in place.
momTip: Moisturize your belly daily — it may not prevent stretch marks, but it soothes the itch of stretching skin.
partnerTip: Tell her she's beautiful, specifically and often; bodies change fast now and reassurance lands deeply.

headline: Dancing to music
development: Your baby can hear sounds from outside the womb and may startle or move to loud noises and music. The lungs are practicing breathing motions with amniotic fluid.
momTip: Play the songs you love — babies have been shown to recognize music heard in the womb after birth.
partnerTip: Make a playlist for the bump: the songs you want your baby to grow up knowing.

headline: A face like theirs
development: Your baby's face is almost fully formed, complete with eyelashes. The lungs are developing branches and the cells that will produce surfactant, needed for breathing air.
momTip: Glucose screening usually happens in the next few weeks — ask your provider when yours is scheduled.
partnerTip: Offer to drive her to the glucose test and keep her company; the drink is famously unpleasant.

headline: Hands that grasp
development: Your baby's hands are fully developed with a startle reflex and a grip. The nostrils, sealed until now, are beginning to open.
momTip: You may notice Braxton Hicks — practice contractions that feel like a tightening; they soften when you change position.
partnerTip: Learn the difference between Braxton Hicks and real contractions now, so you're both calm later.

headline: Eyes about to open
development: The eyes, fused shut for months, will begin to open soon. Your baby is taking small practice breaths and the lungs keep maturing day by day.
momTip: Your center of gravity is shifting — wear supportive shoes and take stairs a little slower.
partnerTip: Walk beside her at her pace, not yours; evening walks together are good for sleep and for talking.

headline: Dreaming begins
development: Your baby's brain is active enough for sleep cycles — and possibly the first dreams. The lungs and nervous system continue their steady maturing.
momTip: This is the last week of the second trimester; if sleep is getting tricky, a wind-down routine genuinely helps.
partnerTip: Take one chore entirely off her plate this trimester and make it permanently yours.

headline: Third trimester, hello
development: Your baby can blink, cough, and has eyelashes. Brain tissue is developing rapidly, and the eyes may now produce tears.
momTip: Your provider may ask you to start counting kicks — pick a quiet time each day and get to know your baby's rhythm.
partnerTip: Join the evening kick counts; putting your hand on the bump and waiting together is its own ritual.

headline: Muscle and marrow
development: Muscles and lungs keep maturing, and the bones are soaking up calcium by the day. Your baby's head is growing to make room for a rapidly developing brain.
momTip: Calcium-rich foods matter extra now — yogurt, cheese, tofu, and leafy greens all count.
partnerTip: Cook dinner with calcium in mind this week; feeding the pregnancy is a real way to help.

headline: Trading space for strength
development: Your baby is running out of room for acrobatics, so movements feel more like rolls and stretches than kicks. The bone marrow has taken over red blood cell production completely.
momTip: Feeling breathless when you lie flat is normal — prop yourself up with extra pillows.
partnerTip: Build her the pillow fort before she asks; comfort engineering is love in practice.

headline: All five senses online
development: All five senses are working. Your baby can track light, taste what you've eaten, hear your conversations, and respond to touch on the belly.
momTip: Swelling in feet and ankles is common; elevate them when you sit and mention sudden puffiness to your provider.
partnerTip: Foot rubs. Nightly. No further notes.

headline: Soft bones, strong grip
development: Your baby has toenails, fingernails, and real hair — or at least a respectable peach fuzz. The skeleton is fully formed but the bones stay soft and pliable for the journey ahead.
momTip: Many babies settle head-down around now; your provider will check position at upcoming visits.
partnerTip: Start the hospital bag checklist together — having a plan calms both of you.

headline: Walls that glow
development: The walls of the womb have thinned and stretched, letting more light in — your baby can tell day from night. The immune system is receiving antibodies from you.
momTip: Keep up your iron intake; your blood volume has increased by about half since pregnancy began.
partnerTip: Book something lovely for week 36 — a dinner, a day trip — before schedules narrow.

headline: Lungs nearly ready
development: The central nervous system and lungs are maturing rapidly. The protective vernix coating is getting thicker, and fat layers are rounding out your baby's cheeks.
momTip: Rest whenever the tiredness comes — third-trimester fatigue is real and earned.
partnerTip: Handle the logistics this month: car seat research, install date, pediatrician shortlist.

headline: Snug as a seed
development: Your baby is gaining about half a pound a week, and the kidneys and liver are fully functional. The grip is strong enough to hold your finger from day one.
momTip: Appointments likely move to every two weeks now — keep a running list of questions on your phone.
partnerTip: Add your own questions to her list too; you're allowed to be curious and prepared.

headline: The long wiggle down
development: Your baby may begin descending into the pelvis, which can ease your heartburn and sharpen the pressure below. The downy lanugo hair is mostly gone.
momTip: Walking, bouncing on a birth ball, and rest in equal measure — listen to which one your body asks for.
partnerTip: Install the car seat this week and get it inspected; it's the one task with no extension.

headline: Early term, full wonder
development: Your baby is considered early term. The lungs and brain are still fine-tuning, and your baby is practicing breathing, sucking, and gripping all at once.
momTip: Wash the tiny clothes, pack the bag, then let yourself do nothing at all — you've earned the pause.
partnerTip: Keep your phone charged and your calendar flexible from here on out.

headline: Waiting, beautifully
development: Your baby's brain and nervous system are still adding connections — development continues right up to birth. The grasp reflex is strong, and the eyes may be gray-blue for now.
momTip: Note the difference between practice contractions and the real thing: real ones get longer, stronger, and closer together.
partnerTip: Agree on the 'it's time' plan: who you call first, which route you drive, what's in the bag by the door.

headline: Full term, full heart
development: Your baby is full term. The lungs are coated in surfactant, ready for that first breath, and fat continues to build for warmth in the outside world.
momTip: Do one thing this week that's purely for you — a slow breakfast, a favorite film, a long bath while you still can.
partnerTip: Keep showing up in small ways: water refilled, phone charged, shoulders rubbed. Presence is the job now.

headline: Any day, any hour
development: Your baby is fully developed and simply waiting for the right moment. The skull bones remain soft and slightly overlapping, designed for the journey to you.
momTip: Due dates are estimates — most babies arrive within a window on either side, and yours is no exception.
partnerTip: Be her calm. Bring the snacks, make the calls, hold her hand, and get ready to meet your baby.
